Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Barfoot
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver
Date: 02/08/2022
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 75 as introduced would authorize probate courts to preside over proceedings changing the name of certain minors which could increase receipts to the various county treasuries and judge of probates by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of proceedings conducted to change the name of minors.
In addition, this bill could increase the administrative obligations of certain probate judges designated by written standing order from the presiding circuit court judge, to issue elder abuse protection orders by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of proceedings presided over by probate judges.
Tom Whatley, Chairperson
Judiciary

Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Barfoot
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 02/28/2022
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 75 as passed the Senate would authorize probate courts to preside over proceedings changing the name of certain minors which could increase receipts to the various county treasuries and judge of probates by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of proceedings conducted to change the name of minors.
In addition, this bill could increase the obligations of certain probate judges to issue elder abuse protection orders by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of proceedings presided over by probate judges, which could be offset, in whole or in part, by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of elder abuse protection cases heard by the probate court and the applicable fees charged.
Finally, this bill could reduce revenues to the State General Fund, county general funds, and other funds that court fees are distributed to, by an undetermined amount, dependent upon the number of protective placement or other protective services cases are heard in the probate court instead of the circuit court.
Jim Hill, Chair
Judiciary

Committee: State Government
Sponsor: Hatcher
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 03/07/2022
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 186 as passed the Senate could increase the obligations of the Alabama Port Authority by an undetermined amount to allow the Authority to purchase, construct, and operate inland property and facilities, including intermodal and multi-modal facilities. These obligations could be offset by increased fees assessed from the use of any new facilities.
Further, this bill would allow the Authority to issue bonds for the purchase, construction, or improvement of such inland facilities.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government
